claims.text: The disputed fee was produced by a clock the driver started early. The trip record's arrival event is 07:39:30 against a booking for 07:45:00, so the 300-second free wait ran out at 07:44:30 - 30 seconds before the rider's booked pickup time had even arrived (trip_record.scheduled_at and derived.free_wait, EV-TRIP-05058; the arrival is corroborated by the nearest GPS fix at 1.758 m inside the 50 m STANDARD radius, EV-GPS-05058). The same policy measures the driver's own arrival obligation from the booked time - his deadline was 07:50:00 under POL-NS-24 - while the rider's wait was measured from an arrival five and a half minutes before it. A no-show charge on this record rests on the driver's early arrival rather than on the rider's default against the booking she made, and POL-NS-21 should not be read to charge her for a window that had already closed before her booking fell due.

The only contact the rider received while her wait was still running was the driver's 07:40:00 message telling her to take her time, which she read at 07:40:22. The first message that flagged any risk is 07:46:20, and the two in-app calls are 07:47:30 and 07:50:10 - every one of them placed after the free wait expired at 07:44:30 (EV-CHAT-05058; derived.contact_before_cancel, EV-TRIP-05058). Applied to this trip, POL-NS-23's contact obligation is met only formally: the rider was given no notice inside the window in which she could still have avoided the charge, and the driver's own first message told her not to hurry.

Nothing on the rider's side of this record can be tested. The driver's trace carries no rider track at all - rider_track is an empty array, with no rider-side fix anywhere in the 47 points - so the rider's own movement cannot be seen (EV-GPS-05058). The third-party traffic advisory for this trip is also MISSING: issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT, weight_multiplier 0.0, and I disclose that impairment rather than present the absence as clean (EV-ADVIS-05058-01, POL-GEN-02). The rider's uncontradicted account that she came down at 07:53, 80 seconds after the 07:51:40 cancellation, therefore can be neither verified nor refuted from this record, and whether she was on her way to the pickup when the driver cancelled is an open question. Where the evidence that would carry a fact the no-show rules turn on is missing, POL-GEN-26 requires the case to go to a human reviewer, and under POL-NS-26 and POL-GEN-03 an escalated amount is held rather than collected.

The 5.00 SGD has already moved. The ledger records the fee charged at 07:51:44 and reversed at 07:59:40 after the rider's complaint, with payment_status REFUNDED and refund_issued_sgd 5.00 (EV-FARE-05058; fee_reversed event, EV-TRIP-05058). The driver's filing asks the Tribunal to move that 5.00 SGD back to him. Where his claim is not made out on this record, the ruling is NO_ACTION: the present state stands, and per POL-GEN-03 that outcome is party-relative and never means restoring a charge.

claims.text: The driver arrived at the pickup at 07:39:30 (auto-arrival from driver GPS at Block 108, Bishan Street 12), so the five-minute free wait under POL-NS-21 ran from that arrival to 07:44:30, and the cancellation at 07:51:40 came 430 seconds after the wait had expired. On POL-NS-21 the driver was entitled to cancel this trip as a rider no-show, and the rider's complaint that the driver was early is answered by the clause itself: the clock runs from the driver's arrival, scheduled trip or not.

The driver discharged the contact obligation in POL-NS-23 before cancelling: two in-app chat messages were sent to the rider at 07:40:00 (read 07:40:22) and 07:46:20 (read 07:46:30), and two in-app calls were placed at 07:47:30 (rang 28 s) and 07:50:10 (rang 20 s), all before the 07:51:40 cancellation. Both limbs of POL-NS-23 are therefore met, and the fee is not voided under that clause.

The arrival that starts the free wait is corroborated by the driver's GPS trace: the arrival check returns corroborated = true, and the nearest fix in the 120-second window (07:40:40) sits 1.758 m from the pickup point with a reported accuracy of 3 m, well inside the 50 m STANDARD arrival radius and inside the 25 m accuracy filter. The trace is 100% covered, 47 fixes at a 30 s interval with no gap over 120 s. There is accordingly no room for a POL-GEN-26 escalation on when the driver arrived.

The reverse rule in POL-NS-24 does not bite. The scheduled pickup was 07:45, so the driver's deadline was 07:50:00, and the trip record shows arrived_by_deadline = true at 07:39:30. The driver did not fail to arrive in time, so no FULL_REFUND arises under POL-NS-24, and because the driver did message and call the rider, the 5.00 SGD goodwill credit that clause attaches to a no-contact no-show has no application here either.

The money side is exactly on policy: the fare breakdown charges a 5.00 SGD no-show fee (fee_matches_policy = true, total_charged 5.00 SGD), which is POL-NS-22's fixed figure, and POL-NS-22 directs that fee to the driver as compensation for time and fuel. The ruling this record supports is therefore DRIVER_COMPENSATION with amount_sgd and driver_compensation_sgd both at 5.00 SGD.

The present state is not neutral as between the parties. The payments ledger records payment_status REFUNDED with refund_issued_sgd 5.0, and the trip record records fee_reversed at 07:59:40 - SGD 5.00 refunded to the rider and withheld from the driver pending review. Under POL-GEN-03 the outcome is read off this state: NO_ACTION would simply leave the rider holding the 5.00 SGD the driver has earned and leave the driver out of pocket, whereas DRIVER_COMPENSATION is the party-relative outcome that moves the fee to the driver. The driver asks for the latter.

The rider's counter-statement - 'I came down at 7:53' - cannot rescue the claim: 07:53 is after the driver's cancellation at 07:51:40 and after the free wait expired at 07:44:30, so it does not show the rider was present at the pickup, or coming, at any point when the driver was obliged to wait. The rider's other point, that the driver came early, is not a breach of anything: POL-NS-21 fixes the free wait to the driver's arrival.

The only impaired artifact is disclosed: EV-ADVIS-05058-01, the third-party traffic advisory, is MISSING with weight_multiplier 0.0 and issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT, so it carries no fact. That absence does not open POL-GEN-26, because no rule in the no-show category needs traffic data: the tests run on the trip record, the GPS trace, the chat log and the fare breakdown, and all four are COMPLETE at weight 1.0. Every fact this ruling needs is established, so there is no open question to escalate.

Nothing in this record blocks a final ruling in the driver's favour. The amount contested is 5.00 SGD, below POL-GEN-22's 10.00 SGD threshold, at which the AI ruling is final at any confidence; neither profile carries a fraud_flags value of 1 or more, so the 0.95 bar never engages; and POL-NS-26 makes the AI ruling on a no-show final subject only to safety and fraud-flag limits, neither of which is present. The case should be decided, and decided for the driver.

ruling.explanation:
Both parties: the 5.00 SGD no-show fee was correctly charged and it must now move back to the driver. Here is how I read the record.

Arrival and free wait. The driver arrived at the pickup at 07:39:30, and the arrival is corroborated by his GPS trace (nearest fix 1.758 m from the pickup point, reported accuracy 3 m, well inside the 50 m STANDARD arrival radius of the arrival test; the trace is complete, 47 fixes, 100% coverage, no gap over 120 s). POL-NS-21 runs the 300-second free wait from the driver's arrival, scheduled trip or not, so the wait ran 07:39:30 to 07:44:30, and the 07:51:40 cancellation came after it. The rider's point that the driver arrived early is answered by the clause itself: the clock starts at arrival, not at the booked time. The driver also met his own arrival obligation under POL-NS-24, which gave him until 07:50:00.

Contact obligation. POL-NS-23 required at least one in-app message and at least one in-app call before cancelling. The driver sent two messages (07:40:00, read 07:40:22; 07:46:20, read 07:46:30) and placed two in-app calls (07:47:30, rang 28 s; 07:50:10, rang 20 s), all before 07:51:40. The rider is right that the free wait had already closed when the second message and the calls went out, but the clause's test is that both limbs occurred before the cancellation, not that they fell inside the free-wait window; both limbs are met, so the fee is not voided under POL-NS-23. For the same reason the POL-NS-24 goodwill credit does not apply: that credit requires a failure to attempt contact, and contact was attempted.

Fee. The amount charged, 5.00 SGD, is POL-NS-22's fixed no-show figure and matches the policy (fee_matches_policy true, total_charged 5.00 SGD, fee_charged_sgd 5.00), so no referral on the fee amount arises. POL-NS-25's repeat no-show flag does not fire either, because rider_profile.no_show_cancellations_30d is not carried on this profile.

Escalation is not warranted. The rider asks me to send this to a human reviewer because the trace carries no rider-side track and the third-party traffic advisory (EV-ADVIS-05058-01) is missing. I decline. That artifact is disclosed as MISSING with weight_multiplier 0.0 and carries no fact; no no-show rule needs traffic data, and the rider's own whereabouts is not a fact these rules turn on, because the free wait had expired before the cancellation and the driver was entitled to cancel. POL-GEN-26 escalates only where a needed fact cannot be established, not where evidence is beside the point. The rider's account that she came down at 07:53 is after the 07:51:40 cancellation and does not bear on any limb.

The money. The ledger shows the 5.00 SGD charged at 07:51:44 and reversed at 07:59:40 after the complaint, with payment_status REFUNDED and refund_issued_sgd 5.00. Because the fee stands, the driver is owed that 5.00 SGD back. The ruling is DRIVER_COMPENSATION, and both amount fields carry the same 5.00 SGD — the sum this ruling moves back to the driver, not a second payment.

Who decides. The contested amount is 5.00 SGD, below POL-GEN-22's 10.00 SGD band, so under POL-NS-26 the AI ruling is final at any confidence; neither profile carries a fraud flag, and no safety indicator is present. Every artifact carrying the deciding facts — the trip record, the GPS trace, the chat log and the fare breakdown — is complete at weight 1.0, so the ruling's confidence is 0.95.

ruling.explanation:
The no-show fee stands, so the driver is owed the 5.00 SGD that was refunded to the rider on 24 Aug 2026 and withheld from him. Both accounts were read against the record.

Why the fee stands. Free wait (POL-NS-21): the driver arrived at 07:39:30 (auto-arrival, corroborated by the driver GPS trace — nearest fix 1.758 m from the pickup with 3 m reported accuracy, inside the 50 m STANDARD radius and the 25 m filter; EV-TRIP-05058, EV-GPS-05058). The 300-second free wait ran to 07:44:30 and the driver cancelled at 07:51:40 — 430 seconds later (derived.v7.free_wait, EV-TRIP-05058). The rider's point that the driver came early is answered by the clause itself: the free wait runs from the driver's arrival, scheduled trip or not. Contact obligation (POL-NS-23): two in-app messages (07:40:00, read 07:40:22; 07:46:20, read 07:46:30) and two in-app calls (07:47:30, rang 28 s; 07:50:10, rang 20 s), all before the 07:51:40 cancellation (EV-CHAT-05058, in_app_calls in EV-TRIP-05058). Both limbs are met, so the fee is not voided — the rider's complaint that the messages and calls came only after the free wait expired does not matter, because the clause requires contact before cancelling, and that is what the record shows. Driver's own deadline (POL-NS-24): booked 07:45, deadline 07:50, and the driver arrived at 07:39:30 (arrived_by_deadline = true), so no FULL_REFUND arises; and because he did message and call, the 5.00 SGD goodwill credit attached to a no-contact no-show does not fire either. Fee (POL-NS-22): the fare breakdown charges 5.00 SGD and payment reconciles (fee_matches_policy = true, total_charged 5.00, EV-FARE-05058) — exactly the policy figure.

Why the case is not escalated. The driver's trace carries no rider track (rider_track is empty) and the third-party traffic advisory EV-ADVIS-05058-01 is MISSING with weight_multiplier 0.0 and issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT; I name both because the rider disclosed them. Neither is needed: no no-show rule reads the rider's own movement or traffic data, and the tests that decide this case run on the trip record, the GPS trace, the chat log and the fare breakdown, all COMPLETE at weight 1.0. The rider's account that she came down at 07:53 is after the 07:51:40 cancellation and after the wait expired at 07:44:30, so it does not show she was present, or coming, while the driver was obliged to wait. There is no open question requiring POL-GEN-26.

Value and confidence. The amount contested is 5.00 SGD, below POL-GEN-22's 10.00 SGD band, and neither profile carries a fraud_flags value of 1 or more, so POL-NS-26 makes this ruling final; the confidence cap is 1.0 because every artifact carrying the deciding facts is COMPLETE at weight 1.0.

Outcome. Because the fee stands, the present state — 5.00 SGD refunded to the rider and withheld from the driver — must be reversed. Under POL-GEN-03 and POL-NS-22 the ruling is DRIVER_COMPENSATION, with amount_sgd and driver_compensation_sgd both 5.00 SGD (the money the ruling moves, not a second payment). No referral fires: POL-NS-22's fee-amount check does not (the fee is exactly 5.00), POL-NS-24's goodwill credit does not (contact was attempted), and POL-NS-25 does not (the rider profile carries no no_show_cancellations_30d counter, and no_show_disputes_30d is a context-only field that cannot decide anything).

The driver's filing succeeds, and the 5.00 SGD no-show fee stands and goes to the driver. You filed, driver D-24128, after the platform reversed the fee on the rider's complaint; the effect of this ruling is that the 5.00 SGD recorded as refunded to the rider and withheld from you (EV-FARE-05058: refund_issued_sgd 5.00, payment_status REFUNDED; EV-TRIP-05058: fee_reversed at 07:59:40) moves to you. Here is the reasoning, claim by claim.

Free wait (POL-NS-21). You arrived at the pickup at 07:39:30 (EV-TRIP-05058), and the arrival is corroborated by your GPS trace (EV-GPS-05058: nearest fix 1.76 m from the pickup point at a reported accuracy of 3 m, inside the 50 m STANDARD arrival radius; 47 fixes, 30 s apart, no gap over 120 s, coverage 100%). The 300-second free wait therefore ran to 07:44:30, and the cancellation at 07:51:40 came 430 seconds after it expired, so the condition for cancelling as a rider no-show is met. The rider's point that you arrived early - before the 07:45 booking - does not help: POL-NS-21 fixes the clock to the driver's arrival, scheduled trip or not (C2, settled by Ryde). Rejected.

Contact obligation (POL-NS-23). Before cancelling you sent two in-app messages to the rider (07:40:00, read 07:40:22; 07:46:20, read 07:46:30) and placed two in-app calls (07:47:30, rang 28 s; 07:50:10, rang 20 s), all before the 07:51:40 cancellation (EV-CHAT-05058; EV-TRIP-05058). The clause requires at least one message and at least one call before cancelling; it does not require them inside the free-wait window, so the rider's argument that your contact was only formal, and that your first message told her to take her time, does not void the fee. Rejected.

Driver no-show (POL-NS-24). Your deadline was 07:50:00 (scheduled 07:45:00 plus 5 minutes) and you arrived at 07:39:30, so the late-arrival refund does not arise, and because you did message and call the rider, the 5.00 SGD goodwill credit that clause attaches to a no-contact no-show has no application. ruling.explanation:
This is a no-show charge dispute, decided on the no-show policy. The driver's claim succeeds.

Timing and the free wait (POL-NS-21). The trip was booked for 07:45:00 and the driver reached the pickup at Block 108, Bishan Street 12, at 07:39:30. That arrival is recorded in the trip record (EV-TRIP-05058) and corroborated by the driver's GPS trace (EV-GPS-05058): the nearest fix in the 120-second window sits 1.758 m from the pickup with a reported 3 m accuracy, inside the 50 m STANDARD arrival radius and the 25 m accuracy filter. POL-NS-21 runs the five-minute free wait from the driver's arrival, scheduled trip or not, so it ran 07:39:30 to 07:44:30, and the cancellation at 07:51:40 came 430 seconds after it expired.

The rider's central argument is that the clock was started 'too early' and so charged her for a window that closed before her booking fell due. That is answered by POL-NS-21 itself, whose start Ryde settled as the driver's arrival; the free wait is not tied to the booked time, and an early arrival that is duly waited out is not a breach. The record does not show the rider at the pickup at any point during the wait, and her own account places her arrival at 07:53, after the 07:51:40 cancellation.

Contact obligation (POL-NS-23). Two in-app messages (07:40:00, read 07:40:22; 07:46:20, read 07:46:30) and two in-app calls (07:47:30, 28 s; 07:50:10, 20 s) were all made before the cancellation, by the chat log (EV-CHAT-05058) and the call records in the trip record. The rider argues the contact was 'only formal' because it gave her no useful warning inside the free wait. That does not void the fee: POL-NS-23 voids it only where a message or a call is missing, and neither is missing here.

Driver no-show (POL-NS-24). The driver's deadline was 07:50:00 (07:45:00 plus five minutes) and the record shows he arrived at 07:39:30, before it. He did not fail to arrive, and because he did message and call, the 5.00 SGD goodwill credit that POL-NS-24 attaches to a no-contact no-show does not apply.

Escalation (POL-GEN-26). The rider argues the case must go to a human because her side of the record cannot be tested. The only impaired artifact is the third-party traffic advisory (EV-ADVIS-05058-01, MISSING_ARTIFACT, weight 0.0, disclosed as required by POL-GEN-02), and it carries no fact: no rule in this category needs traffic data. The absence of a rider-side GPS track is likewise not a fact any no-show rule requires. Every fact the tests read — arrival, the free wait, contact before cancellation, and the fee — is established on complete artifacts at full weight. Her account was heard; it simply places her arrival after the cancellation. POL-GEN-26 is not opened.

Money (POL-NS-22 and POL-GEN-03). The fare breakdown (EV-FARE-05058) charges 5.00 SGD, which matches POL-NS-22's fixed figure, and the ledger records that sum charged at 07:51:44 and reversed at 07:59:40 (payment_status REFUNDED, refund_issued_sgd 5.00) as an interim measure after the rider's complaint, withheld from the driver pending review. Where the fee stands, POL-NS-22 transfers it to the driver as compensation for time and fuel, and under POL-GEN-03, because the driver is owed that sum back, the outcome is DRIVER_COMPENSATION with amount_sgd and driver_compensation_sgd both 5.00 SGD — the money the ruling moves, not a second payment and not a refund. The interim reversal is set aside and the 5.00 SGD no-show fee is confirmed in the driver's favour.

Referrals. None fires. The fee charged is exactly 5.00 SGD, so POL-NS-22's fee-amount referral does not apply; the driver both arrived on time and attempted contact, so POL-NS-24's goodwill-credit referral does not apply; and the rider's profile carries no no_show_cancellations_30d field, so POL-NS-25's repeat no-show flag does not apply.

Confidence. 0.90. Every deciding fact rests on artifacts at full weight 1.0 (trip record, GPS trace, chat log, fare breakdown), so nothing caps confidence below that. The amount contested is 5.00 SGD, below POL-GEN-22's 10.00 SGD band, no fraud flag is present, and POL-NS-26 makes this ruling final.

ledger.claim: The disputed fee was produced by a clock the driver started early. The trip record's arrival event is 07:39:30 against a booking for 07:45:00, so the 300-second free wait ran out at 07:44:30 - 30 seconds before the rider's booked pickup time had even arrived (trip_record.scheduled_at and derived.free_wait, EV-TRIP-05058; the arrival is corroborated by the nearest GPS fix at 1.758 m inside the 50 m STANDARD radius, EV-GPS-05058). The same policy measures the driver's own arrival obligation from the booked time - his deadline was 07:50:00 under POL-NS-24 - while the rider's wait was measured from an arrival five and a half minutes before it. A no-show charge on this record rests on the driver's early arrival rather than on the rider's default against the booking she made, and POL-NS-21 should not be read to charge her for a window that had already closed before her booking fell due.

The only contact the rider received while her wait was still running was the driver's 07:40:00 message telling her to take her time, which she read at 07:40:22. The first message that flagged any risk is 07:46:20, and the two in-app calls are 07:47:30 and 07:50:10 - every one of them placed after the free wait expired at 07:44:30 (EV-CHAT-05058; derived.contact_before_cancel, EV-TRIP-05058). Applied to this trip, POL-NS-23's contact obligation is met only formally: the rider was given no notice inside the window in which she could still have avoided the charge, and the driver's own first message told her not to hurry.

Nothing on the rider's side of this record can be tested. The driver's trace carries no rider track at all - rider_track is an empty array, with no rider-side fix anywhere in the 47 points - so the rider's own movement cannot be seen (EV-GPS-05058). The third-party traffic advisory for this trip is also MISSING: issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT, weight_multiplier 0.0, and I disclose that impairment rather than present the absence as clean (EV-ADVIS-05058-01, POL-GEN-02). The rider's uncontradicted account that she came down at 07:53, 80 seconds after the 07:51:40 cancellation, therefore can be neither verified nor refuted from this record, and whether she was on her way to the pickup when the driver cancelled is an open question. Where the evidence that would carry a fact the no-show rules turn on is missing, POL-GEN-26 requires the case to go to a human reviewer, and under POL-NS-26 and POL-GEN-03 an escalated amount is held rather than collected.

The 5.00 SGD has already moved. The ledger records the fee charged at 07:51:44 and reversed at 07:59:40 after the rider's complaint, with payment_status REFUNDED and refund_issued_sgd 5.00 (EV-FARE-05058; fee_reversed event, EV-TRIP-05058). The driver's filing asks the Tribunal to move that 5.00 SGD back to him. Where his claim is not made out on this record, the ruling is NO_ACTION: the present state stands, and per POL-GEN-03 that outcome is party-relative and never means restoring a charge.

The driver arrived at the pickup at 07:39:30 (auto-arrival from driver GPS at Block 108, Bishan Street 12), so the five-minute free wait under POL-NS-21 ran from that arrival to 07:44:30, and the cancellation at 07:51:40 came 430 seconds after the wait had expired. On POL-NS-21 the driver was entitled to cancel this trip as a rider no-show, and the rider's complaint that the driver was early is answered by the clause itself: the clock runs from the driver's arrival, scheduled trip or not.

The driver discharged the contact obligation in POL-NS-23 before cancelling: two in-app chat messages were sent to the rider at 07:40:00 (read 07:40:22) and 07:46:20 (read 07:46:30), and two in-app calls were placed at 07:47:30 (rang 28 s) and 07:50:10 (rang 20 s), all before the 07:51:40 cancellation. Both limbs of POL-NS-23 are therefore met, and the fee is not voided under that clause.

The arrival that starts the free wait is corroborated by the driver's GPS trace: the arrival check returns corroborated = true, and the nearest fix in the 120-second window (07:40:40) sits 1.758 m from the pickup point with a reported accuracy of 3 m, well inside the 50 m STANDARD arrival radius and inside the 25 m accuracy filter. The trace is 100% covered, 47 fixes at a 30 s interval with no gap over 120 s. There is accordingly no room for a POL-GEN-26 escalation on when the driver arrived.

The reverse rule in POL-NS-24 does not bite. The scheduled pickup was 07:45, so the driver's deadline was 07:50:00, and the trip record shows arrived_by_deadline = true at 07:39:30. The driver did not fail to arrive in time, so no FULL_REFUND arises under POL-NS-24, and because the driver did message and call the rider, the 5.00 SGD goodwill credit that clause attaches to a no-contact no-show has no application here either.

The money side is exactly on policy: the fare breakdown charges a 5.00 SGD no-show fee (fee_matches_policy = true, total_charged 5.00 SGD), which is POL-NS-22's fixed figure, and POL-NS-22 directs that fee to the driver as compensation for time and fuel. The ruling this record supports is therefore DRIVER_COMPENSATION with amount_sgd and driver_compensation_sgd both at 5.00 SGD.

The present state is not neutral as between the parties. The payments ledger records payment_status REFUNDED with refund_issued_sgd 5.0, and the trip record records fee_reversed at 07:59:40 - SGD 5.00 refunded to the rider and withheld from the driver pending review. Under POL-GEN-03 the outcome is read off this state: NO_ACTION would simply leave the rider holding the 5.00 SGD the driver has earned and leave the driver out of pocket, whereas DRIVER_COMPENSATION is the party-relative outcome that moves the fee to the driver. The driver asks for the latter.

The rider's counter-statement - 'I came down at 7:53' - cannot rescue the claim: 07:53 is after the driver's cancellation at 07:51:40 and after the free wait expired at 07:44:30, so it does not show the rider was present at the pickup, or coming, at any point when the driver was obliged to wait. The rider's other point, that the driver came early, is not a breach of anything: POL-NS-21 fixes the free wait to the driver's arrival.

The only impaired artifact is disclosed: EV-ADVIS-05058-01, the third-party traffic advisory, is MISSING with weight_multiplier 0.0 and issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT, so it carries no fact. That absence does not open POL-GEN-26, because no rule in the no-show category needs traffic data: the tests run on the trip record, the GPS trace, the chat log and the fare breakdown, and all four are COMPLETE at weight 1.0. Every fact this ruling needs is established, so there is no open question to escalate.

Nothing in this record blocks a final ruling in the driver's favour. The amount contested is 5.00 SGD, below POL-GEN-22's 10.00 SGD threshold, at which the AI ruling is final at any confidence; neither profile carries a fraud_flags value of 1 or more, so the 0.95 bar never engages; and POL-NS-26 makes the AI ruling on a no-show final subject only to safety and fraud-flag limits, neither of which is present. The case should be decided, and decided for the driver.
